questions.question: A Windows laptop will not be used for a long time, but the user wants to resume the session later. Per the syllabus, which mode is meant for a long period of no use?
questions.explanation: Per the syllabus, Hibernate mode is used when the computer will not be used for a long time, while Sleep mode is for a short time of no use.

questions.question: Binary search with mid = (first + last) // 2 is applied to the sorted list [2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 43] to find key 2. How many iterations are needed?
questions.explanation: Iteration 1: mid = 7 (17), go left. Iteration 2: first 0, last 6, mid = 3 (7), go left. Iteration 3: last 2, mid = 1 (3), go left. Iteration 4: mid = 0, key 2 found.

questions.question: Which HTML code starts a numbered list counting from 3?
questions.explanation: A numbered list is created with <ol>, and the attribute start="3" begins the ordered list at 3. <ul> creates a bulleted list.

questions.question: Which type of RAM uses capacitors to store data and must therefore be refreshed many times per second?
questions.explanation: DRAM uses capacitors and must be refreshed many times per second. SRAM uses transistors, does not need refreshing and is used for cache memory.

questions.question: Which branch of the Theory of Computation studies what makes some problems computationally hard and others easy?
questions.explanation: Computational complexity theory studies what makes some problems hard and others easy. Computability theory asks what can or cannot be computed, and automata theory studies abstract machines.

questions.question: Which assignment creates a tuple containing the single element 20?
questions.explanation: A single-element tuple must include a trailing comma, as in (20,). Without the comma, (20) is just the integer 20; square brackets create a list.

questions.question: In a Bluetooth piconet, a master device can communicate with up to how many active slave devices?
questions.explanation: A Bluetooth master can communicate with up to 7 active slaves. A network may hold up to 255 devices, but only 8 (master plus 7 slaves) communicate at the same time.

questions.question: In Java, the JDK is made up of which components?
questions.explanation: JDK (Java Development Kit) = JRE (Java Runtime Environment) + compilers + debugger. The JDK must be installed to create, compile and run Java programs.

questions.question: In the database hierarchy, a group of related fields forms a:
questions.explanation: In the hierarchy, bytes form fields, a group of fields forms a record, a group of records forms a file/table, and a group of files forms a database.

questions.question: In IoT, what is the main advantage of processing data with edge computing rather than sending everything to the cloud?
questions.explanation: Edge computing processes data close to where it is generated, so its main advantage over cloud processing is reduced latency. It is the technology used for real-time data processing in IoT.

questions.question: Which combination is desirable for a well-designed software module?
questions.explanation: Cohesion measures the functional strength of a module and coupling measures interdependence between modules. Cohesion should be strong and coupling should be low.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about key-based cryptography are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.A: In symmetric-key cryptography, the shared key is called the secret key
options.B: RSA is an example of an asymmetric-key algorithm
options.D: In asymmetric encryption, the receiver decrypts using the public key

questions.explanation: Symmetric systems use a single shared secret key, and RSA is the best example of asymmetric-key cryptography. DES is a conventional symmetric algorithm, and in asymmetric encryption the receiver uses the private key.

questions.question: The Intel 8085 microprocessor has a data bus and an address bus of which widths?
questions.explanation: The 8085 is an 8-bit second-generation CPU (1976) with an 8-bit data bus and a 16-bit address bus. A 20-bit address size belongs to the 8086.

questions.question: Given str1 = 'Hello World!', what does str1[0:10:2] return?
questions.explanation: str1[n:m:k] takes characters from index n up to m-1 in steps of k. Indices 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 give 'H', 'l', 'o', 'W', 'r', so the result is 'HloWr'.

questions.question: MS-DOS is classified as which type of operating system?
questions.explanation: MS-DOS is a single-user, single-tasking OS. Windows and macOS are single-user multi-tasking, while Windows Server and mainframes are multi-user multi-tasking.

questions.question: In an HTML table, what does cell padding specify?

options.A: Gap between one table cell and the next one
options.B: Space between a cell's content and border
options.C: Thickness of the outer table border
options.D: Height of each table row and header

questions.explanation: Cell padding is the space between a table cell's content and its borders, whereas cell spacing is the space between adjacent table cells.

questions.question: Using the remainder method h(element) = element % 10 on a hash table of size 10, which pair of elements causes a collision?
questions.explanation: 26 % 10 = 6 and 46 % 10 = 6, so both map to index 6 and collide. The other pairs give different remainders (2/1, 5/4, 0/1).

questions.question: In Java, which statement correctly describes method overloading?

options.A: Same name and same signature in parent and child, with dynamic binding
options.B: Same name and different signatures in parent and child, resolved at run time
options.C: Same name and different signatures in the same class, with static binding
options.D: Different names but the same signature, resolved during execution

questions.explanation: Overloading uses the same method name with different signatures within the same class, with static binding at compile time. Overriding uses the same name and signature across parent and child classes with dynamic binding.

questions.question: A walkie-talkie lets both users talk, but only in one direction at a time. This mode of data communication is:
questions.explanation: Half-duplex communication is two-way but only one direction at a time, as with a walkie-talkie. Simplex is one-way only, and full-duplex allows simultaneous two-way transfer.

questions.question: Which machine model is described in the syllabus as a type of Turing machine with limited memory?
questions.explanation: A Linear Bounded Automaton is a type of Turing machine with limited memory. Pushdown automata recognize context-free languages, and finite automata recognize only regular languages.

questions.question: A fund transfer debits one account, but the system crashes before the other account is credited, so the whole transaction is rolled back. Which ACID property ensures this all-or-nothing behaviour?
questions.explanation: Atomicity means a transaction is all or nothing. Consistency maintains a valid state, Isolation keeps transactions from affecting each other, and Durability makes committed changes permanent.

questions.question: Which technique provides a one-time session key that two parties can use for secure communication?
questions.explanation: Diffie-Hellman securely exchanges keys and provides a one-time session key for two parties. Steganography hides data inside media such as images rather than exchanging keys.

questions.question: What is the standard port number used by secure MQTT?
questions.explanation: The standard port for secure MQTT is 8883. MQTT is a lightweight machine-to-machine IoT protocol whose messages are secured through SSL/TLS.

questions.question: Which CPU register contains the address of the next instruction to be executed?
questions.explanation: The program counter contains the address of the next instruction to be executed. The accumulator stores intermediate ALU results, and the memory buffer register holds the content of the accessed memory word.

questions.question: An existing application is modified so that it runs on a newly adopted operating system, without adding any new features. Which type of maintenance is this?
questions.explanation: Adaptive maintenance updates software to fit a new environment. Perfective maintenance adds new features to existing software.
